title: Fix Stacked Tab Active Chrome
description: When two tabs are stacked in mode dock, window chrome breaks: active mark draws across full width, body frame missing. Fix multi-tab ModeDockTabBar/ModeDockStack layout so active primary stroke wraps only active tab+body column.
summary: Made the stacked-tab active chrome read as one continuous outline. Root cause of the gap mark 'flowing on top': the `min-h-medium` CSS utility was never defined (only `min-h-huge` existed), so the empty canvas gap between the tab stack and the fullscreen control collapsed to 1px and its `border-b` active stroke rendered at the TOP of the header. Fixes: (1) added the missing `min-h-tiny/small/medium/large` utilities in ui/styling/js/ui.css; (2) gave the grid gap cell `flex items-stretch` so the gap div fills the header row and its red baseline sits at the BOTTOM (verified live: gap was top=35/bottom=36, i.e. 1px); (3) inactive sibling tabs now carry a per-stack bottom baseline (`border-b-active-base` when the stack is globally active, else `border-b-element`) instead of `!border-b-0`, so the active outline runs continuously along the bottom of the inactive tabs left of the active tab and connects into the active tab cap, gap baseline, and fullscreen cap. Extended the 'Mode tab stack places body under active tab and gap only' test to assert the gap cell is flex/items-stretch, the inactive tab has the active bottom baseline (no border-b-0), and the active tab keeps border-active-base + border-b-0. All 62 @semio-tech/ui-react tests pass. Note: could not visually confirm in the running renderer because a concurrent UNIFIED-RENDERER-NEUTRAL-STORE-ABSTRACTION refactor currently renders the cad play shell blank; ground-truth was confirmed via DOM computed styles before the refactor and via unit tests after.
